neighbours.label: the contrastive 'It's one thing (to/for) X' construction, which sets up 'and another (thing) to Y', as opposed to a literal count of one thing
fire: Critics say it is one thing to pass a law and quite another to enforce it.
Writing the code is one thing. Keeping it running for years is another.
It's one thing for adults to take that risk, but children cannot choose.
Buying a boat is one thing; maintaining it every winter is another matter.
For the coach, it was one thing to lose, and another to lose without a fight.
Learning the rules is one thing, but playing well under pressure is harder.
It is one thing for a student to forget homework once; it is another to never do it.
Winning the election was one thing. Governing the country proved far harder.
quiet: Critics say there is one thing the new law does well: it is short.
Before you go, remember one thing: lock the back door.
She packed only one thing for the trip, a small blue bag.
There is just one thing missing from the recipe, and that is salt.
For the coach, the only thing that mattered was the final score.
He could not find a single thing to eat in the fridge.
The one thing every student needs is a quiet place to work.
Winning the election was the main thing on his mind all year.
